Q: Correctly parse "formula" object in R A:

The tree structure of the formula breaks down as follows:

  • top level: ~( y, response)

Internally, this is a list-like object where the first element is the operator (~), the second element is the first argument, and the third element is the third argument.

So deparse(fo[[2]]) gets you "y"

  • next level (response): | (x1+x2, 0 + ...). Same general structure (first element is the operator |, second element is the first arg, third element is the second arg)

so fo[[c(3,2)]] gets x1+x2.

all.vars(fo[[c(3,2)]])

gets the variables to the left of the bar

all.vars(fo[[c(3,3)]])

gets the variables to the right of the bar

This gets considerably trickier if you want to extract terms rather than variables; for example all.vars(quote(log(x)) gets "x", not "log(x)"

Possibly useful, you can also use lobster::ast() to display the abstract syntax tree (AST):

> lobstr::ast(y ~ x1 + x2 | 0 + z1 + z2 + z3 + z4 + z5)
█─`~` 
├─y 
└─█─`|` 
  ├─█─`+` 
  │ ├─x1 
  │ └─x2 
  └─█─`+` 
    ├─█─`+` 
    │ ├─█─`+` 
    │ │ ├─█─`+` 
    │ │ │ ├─█─`+` 
    │ │ │ │ ├─0 
    │ │ │ │ └─z1 
    │ │ │ └─z2 
    │ │ └─z3 
    │ └─z4 
    └─z5

@bathyscapher points out that the terms function might be useful, but in this case I don't think terms(fo) has very much that's useful to you; the bar (|) actually seems to confuse it considerably.

fo <- y ~ x1 + x2 | 0 + z1 + z2 + z3 + z4 + z5

Q: Kalman filter with different sampling rate A:

Your process model should depend on the timestep (call it dt). Then you run a loop. You predict while you have odometry. You have a state estimate for each timestep k.

Then you do a correction step (that I assume you are using the LiDAR for). If the timesteps do not coincide, you compute the dt between your last prediction and the timestep at which you are correcting. You add a state at that timestep. You predict, then immediately correct.

So the key is that your discrete-time process model is actually timestep dependent and you need to handle this explicitly. For some examples you can take a look at https://github.com/decargroup/navlie/blob/main/examples/ex_ekf_vector.py , where this is handled. (So check the way the predict/correct structure is and the actual code for the filter).
